base_properties.human_readable: Genesis 1-2 as ANE Literary Framework (Non-Cosmological Reading)

stakeholders.name: academic_biblical_scholarship
stakeholders.situation: Interprets Genesis 1-2 through source criticism, form criticism, and ANE literary parallels (Enuma Elish, creation myths from Mesopotamia, Egypt). Maintains that the text employs ancient cosmological structures without making empirical cosmological claims. Controls academic publishing, university curricula, and seminary training in historical-critical methodology. Defines what counts as legitimate biblical scholarship and what remains 'fundamentalist' outside that frame. Gains professional authority and interpretive gatekeeping from this reading.

stakeholders.name: science_education_institutions
stakeholders.situation: Benefits from the reading's disentanglement of theology from cosmology: Genesis becomes culturally valuable narrative, not competing empirical claim. Science classes can teach evolution without the institutional conflict this reading resolves. Avoids the regulatory burden and curriculum-design friction of teaching literal creation alongside fossil evidence. Gains institutional coherence by compartmentalizing Genesis as 'cultural artifact' and evolution as 'empirical science.'

stakeholders.name: fundamentalist_theological_communities
stakeholders.situation: Understand Genesis 1-2 as divine revelation describing actual events in sequential, literal time. The reading displaces their textual authority: Genesis becomes 'just' ancient literature employing cultural conventions, not God's direct account. Their interpretive tradition is reclassified as naive literalism, removed from legitimate biblical scholarship, and isolated from institutional pulpits, seminaries, and academic discourse. Exit would require abandoning the identity commitment that Genesis is revealed truth about actual creation — a fusion of theological belief and hermeneutical method that makes exit existentially costly.

stakeholders.name: young_earth_creationists
stakeholders.situation: Base creation chronology on literal Genesis genealogies and day-counts, placing creation ~6000-10000 years ago. The reading directly contradicts their computational framework: if Genesis employs ANE literary convention rather than linear genealogy, their chronological reconstruction collapses. They face institutional pressure (exclusion from mainstream scholarship, loss of credibility in educational settings) and internal pressure (cognitive dissonance with evolutionary evidence). Exit means adopting theistic evolution or science-accommodation, which many experience as capitulation to secular authority.

stakeholders.name: evangelical_accommodationists
stakeholders.situation: Desire theological authority for Genesis (belief in revelation) while accepting evolutionary cosmology. The reading provides institutional tools: they can teach their children 'Genesis is theologically true but not scientifically literal' without losing the text's authority-status entirely. Yet they face constant tension with communities that see this as half-measure compromise; the reading's success depends on accepting that Genesis is 'cultural artifact' — which many find theologically diminishing. They enjoy some benefits (academic respectability) but pay the cost of delegitimized literalism within their own tradition.

stakeholders.name: mainline_protestant_seminaries
stakeholders.situation: Train clergy using historical-critical methods and the ANE literary framework reading. Define what counts as theologically educated vs. fundamentalist. Control pulpit authority: mainline pastors teach Genesis as literature/theology; fundamentalist pastors teach it as literal history. The reading sustains their institutional gatekeeping and professional identity as 'theologically sophisticated.' They maintain the constraint actively through curriculum design, accreditation standards, and pulpit authority.

stakeholders.name: secular_academy
stakeholders.situation: Benefits from the reading's theoretical separation of theology from natural philosophy: evolution becomes unchallengeable empirical science; Genesis becomes culturally interesting text outside the domain of empirical claims. The conflict is intellectually dissolved rather than empirically adjudicated. Analytical seat; does not enforce, but the reading reduces institutional friction between religious and scientific authority.

stakeholders.name: excluded_literal_interpreters
stakeholders.situation: Home-schooling families, independent congregations, and lay Bible study groups who read Genesis literally and teach creation timelines to their children. Not invited to, not considered legitimate participants in, scholarly conversation about what Genesis means. Their interpretive tradition is pre-sorted into 'unscholarly' and their voices absent from curriculum-setting, seminary training, and institutional theology. They would argue that the ANE literary framework reading misrepresents the text's own self-presentation as revelation and history, but that objection enters no institutional forum where it could challenge the reading's dominance.

stakeholders.name: analytical_observer
stakeholders.situation: Documents how the reading redistributes interpretive authority: from revelation-based hermeneutics to historical-critical method; from theological communities' self-interpretation to academic gatekeepers' institutional definitions; from literalist communities' lived reading practices to scholarly consensus about what 'really counts' as legitimate interpretation.

six_questions.coordination_function: Resolves institutional conflict between evolutionary cosmology and theological authority by repositioning Genesis outside the domain of empirical claims: the text becomes a culturally transmitted narrative employing ancient literary convention, freed from the demand that it describe actual sequential events. This separates theology ('what does it mean religiously?') from natural philosophy ('what is the actual history of the universe?') and permits both to coexist in education and institutional life without logical collision.
six_questions.transfer_function: Transfers hermeneutical authority from literalist theological communities to academic biblical scholarship; interpretive gatekeeping power from lay Bible readers to historical-critical specialists; credibility and institutional legitimacy from young-earth and fundamentalist interpretations to ANE-framework scholarship; public discourse authority over Genesis's meaning from religious communities to secular academic institutions.
six_questions.absent_voices: Literal interpreters (fundamentalist communities, home-schooling families, independent congregations) whose hermeneutical traditions are pre-classified as naive and excluded from legitimate scholarly conversation; they would argue that the text's own framing — 'God said,' sequence-marked days, genealogies presented as genealogies — presents itself as revelation and history, not as cultural artifact employing convention. Literalist exegetes would object that the reading confuses 'the text employs ancient literary conventions' with 'the text makes no historical claims' — that Genesis can authentically employ ANE cosmological schema AND describe actual events (literary form and historical reference are not mutually exclusive). These objections remain unheard in institutional forums.
six_questions.disappearance_rationale: Religious communities would rearrange: literalist theology would recover institutional authority; fundamentalist seminaries would return to direct genealogical reading; young-earth chronology would no longer require academic self-defense. Academic scholarship would be forced to re-engage literalist interpretation rather than dismissing it beforehand as theologically naive. The institutional conflict would resurface rather than being resolved by categorical separation. Yet secular academy might see little change — evolutionary cosmology would persist unchanged; the intellectual separation of theology from natural philosophy would dissolve, not end.
six_questions.founding_problem: By the 19th-20th centuries, evolutionary geology and biology made the literal chronologies of Genesis (young earth, sequential creation days, genealogical calculation) empirically untenable. Theological institutions faced a choice: either revise Genesis interpretation (accommodate to science) or oppose evolutionary science (defend Genesis literalism). The ANE literary framework reading emerged as a third path: Genesis uses ancient literary conventions and employs ANE cosmological schema WITHOUT making empirical cosmological claims, thus Genesis is not in competition with evolutionary science at all — the text makes theological, not cosmological, assertions.
six_questions.founding_problem_corroboration: Academic biblical scholarship and evolutionary biologists attest the founding problem was real and the reading solves it (institutional conflict resolves when categories are separated). Mainline seminaries and science educators attest the coordination benefit persists (textbooks and curricula now teach both without friction). However, literalist interpreters contest the diagnosis: they argue the founding problem was wrongly defined — Genesis does make historical claims, and the proper response is either to question evolutionary premises OR to accept that Genesis describes real events using narrative form available in ancient literature. They attest that the reading did NOT solve the conflict but merely declared literalists out of bounds. No voice outside the reading's beneficiary coalition corroborates the founding problem's resolution as conclusively settled.

commentary.narrative_context: Genesis 1-2 exists within a contested kernel about cosmological truth and theological authority. This constraint instantiates one reading: the text employs Ancient Near Eastern cosmological schema and literary conventions (narrative framing, genealogical structures, mythological motifs paralleled in Enuma Elish and Mesopotamian creation stories) WITHOUT making empirical cosmological claims about the actual age of the earth or the sequential mechanism of creation. Under this reading, Genesis is theologically meaningful — it makes claims about God's relationship to creation, humanity's place in the world, and humanity's dependence on divine intent — but not cosmologically prescriptive. The constraint operates as a tangled rope: it coordinates resolution of institutional conflict between evolutionary science and theological authority (genuine coordination benefit for secular academia and science education) while simultaneously extracting hermeneutical authority from literalist theological communities and repositioning their interpretation as naive and out-of-bounds (asymmetric extraction). The reading is actively enforced through academic gatekeeping, curriculum standards, and institutional credentialing.
key_agents: Academic biblical scholarship — institutional agenda-setter and beneficiary; controls what counts as legitimate interpretation and who gets pulpit/classroom authority
Science education institutions — organized beneficiary; gains institutional coherence by compartmentalizing Genesis as theology and evolution as empirical science
Fundamentalist theological communities — organized payer, identity-locked; face displacement of their textual hermeneutics and institutional isolation
Young-earth creationists — moderate-power payer, identity-locked; base cosmology on Genesis genealogies now reframed as literary convention
Evangelical accommodationists — moderate payer/beneficiary; gain tools to hold Genesis authority while accepting evolution, but at cost of delegitimized literalism
Mainline seminaries — institutional agenda-setter and beneficiary; define what counts as theologically educated and maintain gatekeeping
Secular academy — institutional beneficiary; benefits from theoretical separation of theology and natural philosophy
Literal interpreters (excluded) — powerless, excluded; their hermeneutical objections do not enter institutional conversation
commentary.logic_rationale: Extractiveness (0.67) reflects that the reading's persistence depends on active enforcement of hermeneutical authority transfer. The constraint is not self-sustaining through participant preference — literalist communities have not voluntarily adopted the ANE framework; they have been displaced. Measurement series show gradual rise from 0.42 to 0.67 over the 40-unit interval, tracking increasing institutionalization: as mainline seminaries standardize the reading, as universities adopt it in curriculum, as scholarship citations enforce it as baseline assumption, extractiveness rises. Suppression (0.72) is high because the constraint's persistence requires active exclusion of literalist interpretation from legitimate scholarly conversation — alternatives must be pre-sorted into 'fundamentalist' and kept at institutional distance. Theater ratio (0.58) reflects that substantial enforcement activity is devoted to defending hermeneutical authority rather than engaging the text's own self-presentation: scholars defend 'we now understand what the text really is' rather than asking whether the text presents itself as revelation and history. The rising theater ratio (0.35 → 0.58) tracks increasing emphasis on meta-interpretive gatekeeping (defining what counts as scholarship) over direct textual exegesis.
commentary.perspectival_gap: From the academic-beneficiary seat, the constraint is intellectual clarification that resolves conflict. From the payer seats (literalist communities), the constraint is institutional coercion that invalidates their hermeneutics through professional gatekeeping and redefines their interpretation as naive. The engine computes per-seat types from power, exit, and beneficiary/victim status; the claim/metric gap is intentional — the constraint is CLAIMED as tangled_rope (genuine coordination benefit for science education + asymmetric extraction of hermeneutical authority), and the metrics support that claim. Where computed types diverge from the claim, that divergence is the measurement the framework is meant to take.
commentary.directionality_logic: Academic scholarship (d ≈ 0.1): institutional power, arbitrage-grade exit options, chief beneficiary — no cost, full benefit. Science institutions (d ≈ 0.2): organized power, institutional scope, clear beneficiary from separation of domains. Fundamentalist communities (d ≈ 0.85): organized power but constrained within their own institutional sphere, identity-locked exit (rejecting literalism requires rejecting fused religious identity), victims of hermeneutical displacement. Young-earth creationists (d ≈ 0.80): moderate power, biography-scale time horizon, identity-locked exit, directly contradicted by the reading's cosmological reframing. Evangelical accommodationists (d ≈ 0.55): moderate power, constrained exit, benefit from theological tools but pay cost through internal delegitimation. The asymmetry is structural: beneficiary seats have arbitrage-grade mobility and institutional power; payer seats have identity-locked exit and institutional isolation.
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: The founding problem (19th-century collision between Genesis literal reading and evolutionary science) remains contested in its resolution. Academic scholarship and science education attest the problem is solved: Genesis is cultural artifact, not cosmological claim, conflict disappears through categorical separation. However, literalist communities dispute this diagnosis — they argue the reading did not solve the conflict but merely excluded them from institutional conversation. A genuine mandatrophy would be: the reading's founding function (resolve evolutionary-theological conflict) becomes inaccessible to newer generations of readers because the institutional mechanism for enforcing the separation (academic gatekeeping, seminary curricula, textbook standards) becomes invisible or degraded. The disappearance_verdict should be contested because fundamentalist and young-earth communities would argue the constraint does NOT disappear if removed — their theological systems would rearrange, recovering institutional authority they currently lack. Yet secular academy might see little change. The founding problem's status (contested) tracks this: beneficiary seats (science, academia) attest it is dead and the reading solved it; payer seats (literalists, creationists) attest it is live and the reading did not solve it but suppressed it. This is precisely the scenario where mandatrophy is ambiguous — the constraint persists not because all parties agree it solves a problem, but because one party has institutional power to enforce the reading as authoritative.
commentary.kernel_context: This constraint instantiates ONE reading of the kernel 'Genesis creation cosmology.' The kernel is a fixed text (Genesis 1-2) that multiple interpretive traditions claim to legitimately instantiate. This reading asserts that Genesis employs ANE literary conventions and cosmological schema WITHOUT making empirical cosmological claims — the text is culturally meaningful but not scientifically prescriptive. Sibling readings instantiate the same kernel differently: 'young_earth_literal' asserts Genesis describes actual sequential creation events occurring ~6000-10000 years ago; 'theistic_evolution' asserts Genesis describes theological truth through non-literal forms compatible with evolutionary cosmology. The three readings are held simultaneously by different communities (coexist_with relation), not successive refinements of a single tradition. The structural delta of this reading: both scientific authority (evolution is unchallengeable empirical fact) and traditional theological authority (Genesis is revealed truth) are displaced — the text becomes a cultural artifact interesting to scholars but not normatively binding on cosmological or theological questions.

omegas.question: Does identifying ancient literary convention in Genesis establish that the text makes no historical claims, or can a text employ ancient literary form AND describe actual events?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Examine whether other ancient texts employing similar forms (Egyptian records, Mesopotamian king lists) are treated as historical sources or purely mythological. Compare how scholars classify texts that use narrative frames but describe verifiable events. Assess whether 'uses ancient convention' logically entails 'makes no historical claims' or whether the two are independent properties.
omegas.impact: If texts can employ ancient convention while remaining historical, the reading's inference (convention → no historical claims) is invalid, and Genesis could be both literarily conventional AND cosmologically descriptive. If convention strictly implies mythological rather than historical function, the reading's classification stands. This is the hinge on which literalist objections turn.
omegas.description: Whether ancient literary form logically precludes historical reference.

omegas.question: Is the reading's institutional dominance driven by genuine intellectual coherence of the ANE framework, or by academic institutional power structure that can afford to exclude rival interpretations?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Track whether literalist scholars with PhDs and institutional credentials can publish in mainstream biblical scholarship venues. Measure access to seminary teaching positions, academic conferences, and peer-reviewed journals by interpretive tradition. Survey whether the gatekeeping exclusion is justified through explicit methodological standards or through institutional authority assertions ('we now understand...').
omegas.impact: If the reading dominates because it is intellectually superior and more explanatorily powerful, it is a genuine coordination victory (the field converged on better understanding). If it dominates through institutional gatekeeping that excludes credentialed rivals, the extraction component is more salient — the constraint persists through suppression, not through consensus. This is the key for determining whether it is tangled_rope (coordination + extraction) or snare (extraction with coordination cover).
omegas.description: Whether institutional dominance reflects intellectual coherence or gatekeeping power.

omegas.question: Is the resistance of literalist communities to the ANE reading driven by theological principle (Genesis is genuinely revealed truth, and reinterpreting it is theological betrayal) or by identity fusion (the community's self-understanding IS literalist Genesis interpretation)?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Distinguish through narrative analysis and exit tracking: do exit-stage people retain belief in Genesis revelation while adopting ANE reading (principle can survive identity switch), or do they experience the reading adoption as identity dissolution (the identity and the principle are inseparable)? Survey ex-fundamentalists on whether they believe Genesis ceased being God's word or whether they believe they misunderstood how God spoke.
omegas.impact: If identity-locked (principles inseparable from community identity), exit from the reading is existentially costly — the constraint's suppression metric should be higher and persistence should not rely on voluntary adoption. If principle-locked (theological conviction separable from community identity), exit is available and the constraint's persistence depends on genuine belief, not identity fusion. This determines whether the payer seats' resistance is rational conviction or internalized suppression.
omegas.description: Whether literalist exit resistance is theological principle or fused identity.

omegas.question: Are the three readings (literary_framework, theistic_evolution, young_earth_literal) genuinely incommensurable (each instantiating the same kernel via different framings), or does one reading's acceptance logically foreclose another?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Test whether a single scholarly community can hold (a) Genesis uses ANE form and makes no cosmological claims AND (b) God's actual creation occurred through evolutionary mechanisms — both within a single theological framework. Test whether literalism and theistic evolution can coexist in the same seminary or denomination. Assess whether acceptance of 'genre is convention' necessarily forecloses 'actual events occurred in literal sequence.'
omegas.impact: If the readings coexist (different communities hold them simultaneously, neither logically rules out the other), they are in `coexists_with` relation and all remain live readings. If one reading logically forecloses another (genre convention → no historical claims → young_earth is impossible), the relation is `forecloses` and the foreclosed reading's persistence becomes a matter of institutional exclusion rather than live theological debate. This affects the classification: if foreclosed, the reading is more extractive (it doesn't permit rival claims); if coexisting, the reading is more coordinating (it carves out space for different communities).
omegas.description: Whether kernel readings logically foreclose each other or coexist as live positions.

omegas.question: Does secular academia's benefit from the reading's separation of theology and cosmology constitute neutral intellectual arbitration, or is it extraction masked as neutrality?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Track whether secular academy applies the same 'genre-convention-implies-no-claims' analysis to other texts (e.g., whether it treats mythological accounts in scientific contexts as having zero epistemic authority, or whether it selectively applies this only to Genesis). Assess whether the reading arose from internal scholarly developments or from institutional need to resolve curriculum conflict. Measure whether literalist cosmological claims receive the same analytical consideration as evolutionary claims.
omegas.impact: If the reading is intellectually general (genre analysis applies universally), secular academy's benefit is genuine coordination victory. If the reading is strategically applied (only to text that threatens secular authority), the separation is extraction reframed as neutrality — the reading serves the institutional interest of secular academia in monopolizing cosmological authority. This determines whether academia's beneficiary status reflects genuine coordination gain or institutional power consolidation.
omegas.description: Whether academic separation of theology and cosmology is neutral principle or strategic gatekeeping.

network.dual_formulation_note: This constraint is one reading of a three-way contested kernel (genesis_creation_cosmology). The kernel is a fixed text (Genesis 1-2) with three competing interpretive readings: literary_framework (this story), young_earth_literal, and theistic_evolution. Each reading has different beneficiaries, victims, and institutional machinery. The three stories form a constraint family linked by network.affects_constraints. The literary_framework reading specifically forecloses or influences the sibling readings through institutional gatekeeping and hermeneutical authority displacement — but the sibling readings continue to exist as live theological positions held by excluded or marginalized communities. The family structure reveals how the same text can instantiate structurally different constraints depending on which interpretive reading is operant.
